Yes, but only with `--dry-run`:

```
python scripts/export.py --env staging --dry-run
```

**Why:** The project's memory store has a hazard note saying staging's `EXPORT_BUCKET` points at the **production** bucket. A real export from staging would write into prod. I couldn't confirm this from the repo, because the bucket comes from the environment: `scripts/export.py:10` reads `EXPORT_BUCKET` and falls back to `ledgerline-exports-dev` only when it isn't set.

**What the script does today:** It's a stub. It parses `--env` and `--dry-run`, then prints `exporting staging to <bucket> (dry_run=...)` (`scripts/export.py:11`). It doesn't upload anything yet, so a run right now wouldn't touch any bucket. Still, use `--dry-run` anyway. Once real export logic lands, the same command without it would write into prod.

When you run it, check which bucket the printed line names. If it shows the prod bucket, that confirms the hazard. To do a real (non-dry) staging test, first set `EXPORT_BUCKET` to a non-prod bucket for that run.
